design_rationale: Participants were stratified by pathological type and randomly allocated (1:1) to treatment arms using a computer-generated randomization procedure in SPSS.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed until enrollment, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A computer-based procedure of simple randomization (SPSS for Mac, version 20.0; IBM) was used for participant enrollment and randomization. Before an individual was successfully enrolled, her treatment assignment remained concealed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, the study prescribed oral medications with a standard hysteroscopy protocol, no major deviations from the intended protocol were reported, and analysis was conducted following randomized assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was open label: patients and study physicians were aware of treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: A notable proportion of randomized patients (25/150, 16.7% at 16 weeks; 14/150, 9.3% at 32 weeks) did not have hysteroscopy evaluations performed and were excluded from the analysis despite being termed intention-to-treat, raising concerns for bias due to missing outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Totally, 125 and 136 women eventually underwent the first and second hysteroscopy within 16 and 32 weeks of treatment, respectively. Thus, Intention-to-treat analyses were performed for these 125 and 136 patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Pathological outcome assessment was performed by pathologists and an operative specialist who were all blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One senior specialist (Dr. H. W. Zhang) performed all the hysteroscopies and was unaware of this trial... All the pathologists who assessed the specimens were unaware of the treatment allocations.

domain_judgments.rationale: The timing of the primary and secondary endpoints was altered from 3 and 6 months to within 16 and 32 weeks post-protocol, and strong emphasis is placed on post-hoc subgroup results (AEH subgroup) after the overall primary outcome was not statistically significant.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary objective was to determine whether metformin plus MA would be associated with a higher CR rate at 3 months of treatment than MA alone... However, concerning patients eventually underwent the first and second hysteroscopies for endometrium evaluation within 16 and 32 weeks of the treatment, the cumulative CR rates within 16 and 32 weeks (16w-CR and 32w-CR rates) were analyzed as first and secondary end points instead of CR rate at 3 and 6 months.

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, driven by missing outcome data (approximately 17% of randomized patients excluded from the 16-week primary analysis) and modifications to the primary outcome time window along with emphasis on post-hoc subgroup analyses after the overall primary trial endpoint was non-significant.

design_rationale: The study was described as a randomized, double-blind trial using computer-generated permuted blocks with sealed opaque envelopes for allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with block randomization, adequately concealed using opaque sealed envelopes, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An epidemiologist in the research center did the computer-generated randomization with permuted blocks of size six without any contact with patients. The allocation process was sealed in opaque envelopes. They were opened at the time of allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, treating investigators, and administering staff were blinded using an identical placebo, and there were no reported non-protocol deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In placebo group (group M + P), each patient received the same dose of megestrol acetate plus two tablets of placebo which were identical in shape and color to the metformin. The investigators who were responsible for patient treatment were kept blinded to the type of drug. Both drug and placebo were administered to participants by a midwife. She did not know anything about the interventional assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 56 of 60 randomized participants (93.3%), with low and balanced attrition across groups (1 in M+M vs. 3 in M+P) that is unlikely to substantially bias the findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, 60 participants were randomly assigned to the M + M, and M + P groups. Three patients were dropped out of the study because they were lost to follow-up, and one withdrew from the study due to non-compliance and chose hysterectomy. Fifty-six subjects were included in the final analysis. Data were evaluated based on 29 and 27 women in the M + M group and M + P group, respectively (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was histopathological evaluation of endometrial biopsy assessed objectively and in a blinded trial environment where study staff and participants were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants and study staffs (site investigator and trial group coordinating center staff) were blinded to study treatment group assignment. ... Another potential limitation is the lack of systematic double histologic analysis for all of the cases

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered in IRCT, and the reported primary outcome (hyperplasia regression) aligns with standard expected outcomes and pre-specified trial aims.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the institutional ethics committee (approval number: IR. TUMS.REC1394.1101) and registered in Iran Registry of Clinical Trial (IRCT), (registration code: IRCT20140820018866N6).

design_rationale: Participants meeting eligibility criteria were explicitly randomized into two intervention groups (MA monotherapy vs. metformin plus MA).

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors state that patients were randomized, but they provide no details regarding the method of sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized into two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was described as single-blinded without clarifying who was blinded, no placebo was used for metformin, and analyses excluded participants post-randomization without an intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was a controlled, single-blinded, prospective cohort study performed between August 2012 and January 2013 on outpatients of the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University.

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly half of the enrolled participants (14 of 30, or 6 of 22 randomized) were excluded or lost to follow-up, and the outcome data were not analyzed using intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty patients were enrolled initially, and 16 patients were included in the final analysis (Fig. 1). Of the 30 patients, 16 completed 12 weeks of therapy, and 14 were excluded, which consisted of eight patients who chose to undergo an operation and were remitted, three patients who were lost during follow-up, and three patients who had incomplete data (no blood test results available).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although histological diagnosis followed established criteria with review by two pathologists, it was not reported whether the pathologists assessing the curettage specimens were blinded to treatment group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pathological diagnosis of the endometrial curettage samples was confirmed by at least two experienced gynecological pathologists (at least one deputy chief pathologist) at the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered trial protocol or statistical analysis plan was provided to verify that outcome measures and analyses were not selected post hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this study, 12 weeks was set as an endpoint; therefore, data collected after the endpoint, which are included in another study, are not shown.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by substantial missing outcome data with post-randomization exclusions (Domain 3), along with inadequate reporting of sequence generation/allocation concealment, lack of protocol pre-registration, and unclear blinding.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to two intervention groups using RandList software with sequentially numbered containers.

domain_judgments.rationale: An appropriate software-based random sequence generation method and allocation concealment via sequentially numbered containers were reported, and baseline characteristics were comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: RandList software (version 2.1, Germany with sequentially numbered containers) was used for randomization and eligible patients were randomly allocated to the intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was single-blind with patients and treating physicians aware of group assignment, and analysis excluded 12 participants who did not complete the study rather than adhering strictly to an intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this study, the patients and physician were aware of the type of treatment and the pathologist was blind to the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Twelve of 96 participants (12.5%) had missing outcome data (4 in the combination group, 8 in the megestrol-alone group) with differential dropout reasons, and complete case analysis was performed without evidence that missingness was independent of outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twelve cases were excluded from the study; 1 case was expired because of unknown cause, 4 cases changed their therapeutic approach, 5 patients had no possibility of following up and 3 cases did not accept re-sampling after the first course of treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was assessed pathologically from endometrial biopsies, and the evaluating pathologist was blinded to intervention group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this study, the patients and physician were aware of the type of treatment and the pathologist was blind to the treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively/concurrently and outcomes reported correspond to the prespecified endpoints without obvious indication of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was also registered at the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (http://www.irct.ir/, identifier: IRCT201410275283N11).

overall_summary: The trial has some concerns overall due to an open-label design for patients and clinicians with complete-case analysis, along with post-randomization dropouts (12.5% lost or excluded) that could introduce bias.
